items.title: Unramifiedness at a point with a specializing dominant point over a unibranch base implies etaleness
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-morphisms.tex (More on Morphisms)
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-morphisms.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: For a locally finite type morphism over an integral base that is geometrically unibranch at the image point, if there is a specialization from a point lying over the generic point of the base to the given point and the morphism is unramified there, then it is etale there. The proof uses the unibranch hypothesis to control the local structure along the specialization and concludes flatness from unramifiedness plus the dominance condition, giving etaleness. Deriving flatness from the specialization and unibranchness is the load-bearing step. Retained author proof at lines 10479-10493.
